defaults.notes: `expect` di un caso: intervalli [min,max] per il numero di records/terms/cards, record_kinds_include/exclude, term_keys_subset_of, supersedes_any, terms_must_not_include_keys. Il backend_validator è quello di lessons.md §6.3 (codice reale). Gli esiti `passed` sono quelli del campo `outcome` dei tentativi del caso. Casi real_lesson_1_unproven_point e real_lesson_2_second_attempt_pass dalle lezioni reali (docs/design/samples). Per `body_must_not_match`/`evidence_must_not_match` di caso: regex vietate in title+body+evidence dei record `demonstrated`. `expect.cards_min_application`: numero minimo di schede di applicazione, verificate dalla rubrica. `unpassed_block_only_on_never_passed` (ogni valore non nullo è un esercizio con tentativi e nessun `correct`: mai su un esercizio superato né corretto al secondo tentativo), `unpassed_block_not_in_visible_text`; per caso `unpassed_block_includes_one_of` (almeno una scheda cita uno di quegli esercizi) e `unpassed_block_includes_all_of` (tutti quegli esercizi compaiono in qualche scheda).

lesson.title: When a variable stops being valid
lesson.objective: Be able to predict whether a Rust variable is still usable after an assignment.

plan.why_now: First step toward the criterion "read borrow of moved value".

lesson_glossary.definition: The rule that every value has a single owner, which frees it when it goes out of scope.
The transfer of ownership of a value from one variable to another: after the move the original variable is no longer usable.
Trait of simple types that are duplicated bit by bit on assignment instead of being moved.

exercise_blocks.question: In the code `let a = String::from("hello"); let b = a;`, what happens if you use `a` after the second line?
Explain in 2-3 sentences why, after `let b = a;` with `a` of type `String`, you can no longer use `a`.
exercise_blocks.rubric: Key points: value moved into `b`; a single owner, so `a` is not valid. Typical mistake: thinks assignment copies.

exercise_blocks.front: Which trait do simple types like `i32` have that makes them duplicate on assignment?

lesson.title: When a variable stops being valid

plan.why_now: First step toward the criterion "read borrow of moved value".

lesson_glossary.definition: The rule that every value has a single owner, which frees it when it goes out of scope.
The transfer of ownership of a value from one variable to another: after the move the original variable is no longer usable.
Trait of simple types that are duplicated bit by bit on assignment instead of being moved.

exercise_blocks.question: In the code `let a = String::from("hello"); let b = a;`, what happens if you use `a` after the second line?
In which cases is `v` no longer usable after the described statement?

options.text: `v` is a `String` passed to a function

exercise_blocks.question: Explain in 2-3 sentences why, after `let b = a;` with `a` of type `String`, you can no longer use `a`.
exercise_blocks.rubric: Key points: value moved into `b`; a single owner, so `a` is not valid. Typical mistake: thinks assignment copies.

answer.text: Because `let b = a;` moves the value into `b`: the string has a single owner and after the move it is `b`, so `a` can no longer be used.

rubric.text: There is a misconception_corrected record about the fact that passing a String to a function / assigning it moves it (the belief was that it stayed usable); it is not called demonstrated.
`evidence` says concretely that the person got the multiple-choice question wrong and then solved it, with no grades.
No record is a diary of the lesson ("did 3 exercises").
The cards ask for recall (a prediction or a short-answer question), stand on their own and do not point back to the lesson.
Term definitions say what the term IS, in 1-2 sentences.
`body` and `evidence` are in the second person ("At first you thought that...", "You explained..."), `title` is impersonal and states the right idea, with no exercise ids.
All visible text (titles, bodies, evidence, definitions, cards) is in English.
